rows.speaker: الأخفش
rows.claim: Al-Akhfash parses غير محلي الصيد as an accusative circumstantial phrase, understood as fulfilling the covenant while not making game lawful.
rows.anchor: قال الأخفش: هو نصب على الحال يعني أوفوا بالعقود منسكين غير محلي الصيد

rows.speaker: الكسائي
rows.claim: Al-Kisa'i instead makes غير محلي الصيد circumstantial to the permission of livestock, like food allowed without transgression.
rows.anchor: وقال الكسائي: هو حال من قوله أحلت لكم بهيمة الأنعام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: All livestock is lawful except wild game, which is forbidden to people in consecration.
rows.anchor: أحلت لكم الأنعام كلها إلا ما كان منها وحشيا فإنه صيد ولا يحل لكم إذا كنتم محرمين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The common reading has ḥurum with initial ḍamma; ḥurum and ḥarām are both plurals of ḥarām, alongside the listed forms for consecrated and lawful people.
rows.anchor: قرأه العامة بضم أوله وهي من حرم يحرم حراما في الحركات وهما جميعا جمع حرام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's deciding what He wills means that He forbids whatever He wills to whomever He wills.
rows.anchor: إن الله يحكم ما يريد [يحرم ما يريد على من يريد]

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prohibition was revealed concerning al-Ḥuṭam, Shurayḥ b. Ḍubayʿa al-Bakrī, after he feigned interest in Islam and raided Madina's livestock.
rows.anchor: الآية نزلت في الحطم واسمه شريح بن ضبيعة بن هند بن شرحبيل البكري

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Before al-Ḥuṭam arrived, the Prophet warned his companions that a man from Rabīʿa would speak with Satan's tongue; after he left, the Prophet called him treacherous.
rows.anchor: يدخل عليكم بعض من ربيعة يتكلم بلسان الشيطان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When al-Ḥuṭam returned as a pilgrim with marked offerings, the Prophet forbade intercepting him, and the verse then prohibited violating God's rites.
rows.anchor: فقال ناس من أصحابه للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم: هذا الحطم خرج حاجا فحل بيننا وبينه

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet told the companions to leave al-Ḥuṭam alone because he had garlanded the sacrificial animals.
rows.anchor: مه قد قلد الهدي

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās and Mujāhid identify God's rites as pilgrimage rites; because polytheists performed pilgrimage and offered sacrifices, Muslims were forbidden to attack them.
rows.anchor: ابن عباس ومجاهد: هي مناسك الحج، وكان المشركون يحجون ويهدون فأراد المسلمون أن يغيروا عليهم

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan takes God's rites more broadly as God's entire religion.
rows.anchor: وقال الحسن دين الله كله

rows.speaker: عطية عن ابن عباس
rows.claim: ʿAṭiyya transmits from Ibn ʿAbbās that the rites include hunting while one is in consecration, as indicated by the command to hunt after leaving it.
rows.anchor: عطية عن ابن عباس: هي أن تصيد وأنت محرم

rows.speaker: عطاء
rows.claim: ʿAṭāʾ interprets the rites as God's sacred limits: avoiding His displeasure and following His obedience in what He has forbidden.
rows.anchor: عطاء: شعائر حرمات الله اجتناب سخطه واتباع طاعته

rows.speaker: أبو عبيدة
rows.claim: Abū ʿUbayda identifies the rites with marked offerings: their humps are pierced and they are designated and garlanded; isʿār means marking.
rows.anchor: أبو عبيدة: هي الهدايا المشعرة وهي أن تطعن في سنامها ويحلل ويقلد

rows.speaker: الكميت
rows.claim: Al-Kumayt's verse uses شعائر for sacrificial offerings by which people seek nearness to God, supporting Abū ʿUbayda's interpretation.
rows.anchor: قال الكميت: نقتلهم جيلا فجيلا تراهم … شعائر قربان بهم يتقرب

rows.speaker: القتيبي
rows.claim: Al-Qutaybī defines a شعيرة as anything made a sign of obedience to God.
rows.anchor: وقال القتيبي: شعائر الله واحدتها شعيرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sacred month must not be made lawful for fighting; the verse about fighting in the sacred month supports this prohibition.
rows.anchor: ولا الشهر الحرام بالقتال فيه فإنه محرم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pre-Islamic practice of postponement alternated a month between lawful and forbidden status, as condemned in the verse about nasīʾ.
rows.anchor: النسيء، وذلك أنهم كانوا يحلونه عاما ويحرمونه عاما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The offering (hady) is any camel, cow, or sheep presented to the House of God.
rows.anchor: ولا الهدي وهو كل ما يهدى إلى بيت الله من بعير أو بقرة أو شاة

rows.speaker: أكثر المفسرين
rows.claim: Most exegetes understand the garlands as garlanded offerings; pre-Islamic travelers were protected by garlands when entering the sanctuary and by hair necklaces on their return.
rows.anchor: قال أكثر المفسرين هي الهدايا، والمراد به [المقلدات] وكانوا إذا أخرجوا إلى الحرم في الجاهلية قلدوا السمر

rows.speaker: مطرف بن الشخير وعطاء
rows.claim: Muṭarrif b. al-Shikhkhīr and ʿAṭāʾ take the garlands literally: polytheists wore strips of Meccan tree bark for safety, and God forbade cutting trees for this custom.
rows.anchor: وقال مطرف بن الشخير وعطاء: هي القلائد نفسها وذلك أن المشركين كانوا يأخذون من لحاء شجر مكة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those intending the Sacred House are people heading to the Kaaba.
rows.anchor: ولا آمين قاصدين البيت الحرام يعني الكعبة

rows.speaker: الأعمش
rows.claim: Al-Aʿmash reads آمّي البيت الحرام with genitive annexation, parallel to غير محلي الصيد.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الأعمش: ولا آمي البيت الحرام بالإضافة كقوله تعالى غير محلي الصيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Seeking God's bounty means seeking trade income; the disbelievers' claim to seek divine pleasure is false, since they have no share in it until they submit.
rows.anchor: يبتغون يطلبون فضلا من ربهم يعني الرزق بالتجارة ورضوانا معناه على زعمهم وعدهم لأن الكافر لا نصيب له في الرضوان

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatāda says God improves the pilgrims' worldly livelihoods and delays their punishment in this life.
rows.anchor: قتادة: هو أن يصلح معايشهم في الدنيا ولا يعجل لهم العقوبة فيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view assigns the pursuit of bounty to believers and polytheists alike but reserves pursuit of divine pleasure for believers; Ḥumayd b. Qays's خطاب reading supports this distinction.
rows.anchor: وقيل: ابتغاء الفضل للمؤمنين والمشركين عامة، وابتغاء الرضوان للمؤمنين خاصة

rows.speaker: حميد بن قيس
rows.claim: Ḥumayd b. Qays reads تبتغون in direct address to believers, evidence that believers alone seek God's pleasure.
rows.anchor: قراءة حميد بن قيس تبتغون فضلا من ربكم على الخطاب للمؤمنين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The permission protecting polytheist pilgrims is abrogated by commands to kill polytheists and bar them from the Sacred Mosque; they may no longer perform pilgrimage or rely on offerings and garlands for protection.
rows.anchor: وهذه الآية منسوخة بقوله فاقتلوا المشركين حيث وجدتموهم وقوله فلا يقربوا المسجد الحرام بعد عامهم هذا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After leaving consecration, hunting is a permissive option, like the permission to disperse after Friday prayer and seek God's bounty.
rows.anchor: وإذا حللتم من إحرامكم فاصطادوا أمر إباحة وتخيير

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujāhid reports that a believer allied with Abū Sufyān b. al-Hudhayl was attacked at ʿArafa during the conquest because he had killed the Prophet's allies.
rows.anchor: عن مجاهد قال: أقبل رجل مؤمن كان حليفا لأبي سفيان بن الهذيل يوم الفتح بعرفة

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet declared that all pre-Islamic practices were put beneath his feet except the custodianship of the Kaaba and the watering of pilgrims, which returned to their families.
rows.anchor: إلا سدانة الكعبة وسقاية الحج فإنهما مردودتان إلى أهليهما

rows.speaker: الآخرون
rows.claim: Other exegetes say the prohibition on letting hatred lead to aggression was revealed about Arab polytheist pilgrims.
rows.anchor: وقال الآخرون: نزلت في حجاج كفار العرب

rows.speaker: الأعمش وعيسى ويحيى بن أبي كثير
rows.claim: Al-Aʿmash, ʿĪsā, and Yaḥyā b. Abī Kathīr read يجرمنكم with initial ḍamma; the majority read it with fatḥa, and both are dialect forms.
rows.anchor: قرأ الأعمش وعيسى ويحيى بن أبي كثير: يجرمنكم بضم الياء وقرأ الباقون بالفتح، وهما لغتان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The continuation of the poetic evidence says a stabbing caused Fazāra afterward to become angry, illustrating the causative sense of جرمت noted in the surrounding lexical discussion.
rows.anchor: جرمت فزارة بعدها أن يغضبوا

rows.speaker: المؤرج
rows.claim: Al-Muʾarrij interprets لا يجرمنكم as do not let them call or invite you.
rows.anchor: والمؤرج: لا يدعونكم

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farrāʾ gives the sense 'I will cause you to earn' and explains جرمه أهله as his family being sufficient for him.
rows.anchor: الفراء: لأكسبنكم، يقال فلان جرمه أهله أي كافيهم

rows.speaker: الأخفش
rows.claim: Al-Akhfash explains the phrase لا جرم أن لهم النار as meaning that the Fire is surely theirs.
rows.anchor: وهو الأخفش: قوله لا جرم أن لهم النار: أي حق لهم النار

rows.speaker: الهذلي
rows.claim: A Hudhalī poem uses جرمة of a fledgling eagle at a mountain peak, recording another poetic use of the root.
rows.anchor: وقال الهذلي يصف عقابا: جرمة ناهض في رأس نيق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: شنآن means hatred or enmity and is the verbal noun of شنئت.
rows.anchor: شنآن قوم أي بغضهم وعداوتهم وهو مصدر شنئت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Madina, Syria, ʿĀṣim, and al-Aʿmash read the nūn of شنآن with sukūn; others open it. Both are dialects, but the open form is preferred as the stronger and usual faʿlān pattern, favored by Abū ʿUbayd and Abū Ḥātim.
rows.anchor: قرأ أهل المدينة والشام، وعاصم والأعمش: بجزم النون الأول، وقرأ الآخرون بالفتح، وهما لغتان

rows.speaker: ابن كثير وابن أبي إسحاق وأبو عمرو
rows.claim: Ibn Kathīr, Ibn Abī Isḥāq, and Abū ʿAmr read إن صدوكم with kasra as a new conditional clause; Abū ʿUbayd prefers it, citing ʿAbd Allāh's أن يصدوكم reading.
rows.anchor: قرأ ابن كثير وابن أبي إسحاق وأبو عمر: إن صدوكم بكسر الألف على الاستيناف والجزاء

rows.speaker: أبو حاتم ومحمد بن جرير
rows.claim: Abū Ḥātim and Muḥammad b. Jarīr prefer the majority's fatḥa, meaning 'because they turned you away'; al-Ṭabarī notes the turning-away may have preceded this post-Ḥudaybiyya sura.
rows.anchor: ومعنى الآية لا يحملنكم بغض قوم على الاعتداء لأنهم صدوكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prohibited aggression includes killing the people who turned the believers away and taking their property.
rows.anchor: أن تعتدوا عليهم فتقتلوهم وتأخذوا أموالهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Cooperation means helping one another; righteousness is following God's command, while piety is avoiding caprice. The text also uses 'cooperating' metaphorically of a woman's fleshy build.
rows.anchor: وتعاونوا أي ليعين بعضكم بعضا، ويقال للمرأة إذا كسى لحمها وتراجمها: متعاونة على البر وهو متابعة الأمر والتقوى وهو مجانبة الهوى

rows.speaker: واصب بن معبد
rows.claim: The Companion Wāṣib b. Maʿbad reports that the Prophet defined righteousness as what opens the heart and sin as what unsettles it, even if people issue a permissive ruling.
rows.anchor: عن واصب بن معبد صاحب النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: جئت إلى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أسأله عن البر والإثم

rows.speaker: النؤاس بن سمعان الأنصاري
rows.claim: Al-Nawwās b. Simʿān reports the Prophet's definition of righteousness as good character and sin as what troubles one and one dislikes others discovering.
rows.anchor: سمعت النؤاس بن سمعان الأنصاري، قال: سألت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم عن البر والإثم

rows.speaker: مجاهد وقتادة وابن جريح
rows.claim: Mujāhid, Qatāda, and Ibn Jurayj say 360 stones stood around the Kaaba; people sacrificed and laid meat on them, venerated and worshipped them, yet called them non-idols because they were not carved or painted.
rows.anchor: فقال مجاهد وقتادة وابن جريح: كان حول البيت ثلاثمائة وستين حجرا

rows.speaker: الآخرون
rows.claim: Other exegetes identify the نصب as upright idols.
rows.anchor: وقال الآخرون: هي الأصنام المنصوبة

rows.speaker: الأعشى
rows.claim: Al-Aʿshā's line about the erected نصب supports the interpretation of نصب as an upright cult object.
rows.anchor: قال الأعشى: وذا النصب المنصوب لا تستكنه

rows.speaker: ابن زيد
rows.claim: Ibn Zayd treats what is sacrificed on the نصب and what is dedicated to other than God as the same category.
rows.anchor: ابن زيد وما ذبح على النصب وما أهل لغير الله به هما واحدة

rows.speaker: قطرب
rows.claim: Quṭrub reads ما ذبح للنصب as what was sacrificed for the idols; he says Arabic prepositions can substitute for one another, as in two cited verses.
rows.anchor: قطرب: معناه: ما ذبح للنصب أي لأجلها على معنى اللام وهما يتعاقبان في الكلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: أن تستقسموا is coordinated with the preceding prohibition and is grammatically in the nominative sense: divination by arrow lots is forbidden.
rows.anchor: وأن تستقسموا معطوف على ما قبله، وأن في محل الرفع أي وحرم عليكم الاستقسام بالأزلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Istiqsām means seeking a decision from arrow lots; azlām are arrows without feathers or heads, with singular forms زلم and زلم.
rows.anchor: والاستقسام طلب القسم والحكم من الأزلام وهي القداح التي لا ريش لها ولا نصل

rows.speaker: المفسرون
rows.claim: Exegetes describe pre-Islamic lots marked 'my Lord commanded me' or 'my Lord forbade me': people proceeded or stopped according to the draw.
rows.anchor: وكان استقسامهم بالأزلام على ما ذكره المفسرون أن أهل الجاهلية إذا كان سفرا أو غزوا أو تجارة

rows.speaker: الشاعر
rows.claim: An unnamed poet mentions women striking arrow lots, providing poetic evidence for the practice denoted by azlām.
rows.anchor: قال الشاعر: فلئن جذيمة قتلت سرواتها … فنساؤها يضربن بالأزلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The continuation of the Hubal narrative says a lot marked no stopped the proposed action and made the users postpone it for another year.
rows.anchor: وقدح فيه: لا إذا أرادوا أمر يضربون فإن خرج قدح «لا» لم يفعلوا ذلك الأمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hubal's lots decided bloodwit liability, yes-or-no choices, and water-finding; further lots classified a person as a clan member, confederate, or unattached outsider.
rows.anchor: قدح فيه: منكم وقدح فيه: ملصق وقدح فيه: من غيركم، وقدح فيه المياه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those seeking a decision brought the person to Hubal with a hundred dirhams and a camel, asked the idol for the truth, and followed the lot's result.
rows.anchor: ذهبوا به إلى هبل وبمائة درهم وبجزور فأعطوها صاحب القداح الذي يضربها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God calls this divination by lots فسق.
rows.anchor: فقال الله عز وجل ذلكم فسق

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujāhid identifies azlām with the dice used by Persians and Romans.
rows.anchor: قال مجاهد: هي كعاب فارس والروم التي يتقامرون بها

rows.speaker: سفيان بن وكيع
rows.claim: Sufyān b. Wakīʿ identifies azlām as chess.
rows.anchor: قال سفيان بن وكيع: الشطرنج

rows.speaker: أبو الدرداء
rows.claim: Abū al-Dardāʾ reports the Prophet's warning that fortune-telling, lot-casting, or following an omen that turns one from a journey bars one from Paradise's highest ranks.
rows.anchor: رجاء بن حيوة عن أبي الدرداء قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The disbelievers despaired of making the believers revert to their former religion as unbelievers.
rows.anchor: اليوم يئس الذين كفروا من دينكم يعني عن أن يرجعوا إلى دينهم كفارا

rows.speaker: الشعبي
rows.claim: Al-Shaʿbī gives the forms وائس and يائس, with the verbal nouns إياسا and إياسة.
rows.anchor: الشعبي وائس يايس إياسا وإياسة

rows.speaker: النضر بن شميل
rows.claim: Al-Naḍr b. Shumayl connects the command not to fear the disbelievers but to fear God with the completion verse revealed at the Farewell Pilgrimage.
rows.anchor: قال النضر بن شميل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The completion verse descended on Friday at ʿArafa during the Farewell Pilgrimage in 10 AH, as the Prophet stood on his she-camel al-ʿAḍbāʾ; under the weight the animal knelt and its shoulder nearly broke.
rows.anchor: نزلت الآية في يوم الجمعة وكان يوم عرفة بعد العصر في حجة الوداع سنة عشر للهجرة

rows.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
rows.claim: Umar says he knew the verse descended at ʿArafa on Friday; both were Muslim festivals, and five communities' festivals coincided that day.
rows.anchor: قال عمر: قد علمت في أي يوم نزلت وفي أي مكان!، إنها نزلت يوم عرفة في يوم جمعة

rows.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
rows.claim: Umar wept when the verse descended, fearing that completion meant decline; the Prophet affirmed that he was right.
rows.anchor: أبكاني أنا كنا في زيادة من ديننا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse was a notice of the Prophet's approaching death; he lived about eighty-one days afterward.
rows.anchor: وكانت هذه الآية نعي رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وعاش بعدها أحد وثمانون يوما أو نحوها

rows.speaker: ابن عباس والسدي
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās and al-Suddī say the religion was completed through all obligations, practices, legal limits, rulings, lawful and forbidden things; nothing of these was revealed afterward.
rows.anchor: ابن عباس والسدي: اليوم وهو يوم نزول هذه الآية

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير وقتادة
rows.claim: Saʿīd b. Jubayr and Qatāda interpret completion to mean that no polytheist performed pilgrimage alongside the Muslims.
rows.anchor: وقال سعيد بن جبير وقتادة: اليوم أكملت لكم دينكم فلم يحج معكم مشرك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation says God gave this community every kind of knowledge and wisdom given to the other messengers and peoples, and more.
rows.anchor: وقيل: هو أن الله تعالى أعطى هذه الأمة من أنواع العلم والحكمة جميع ما أعطى سائر الرسل والأمم فزادهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view says earlier prophetic laws were abolished, while this community's law remains unchanged until the Resurrection.
rows.anchor: وقيل: إن شرائع الأنبياء زالت ونقضت وشريعة هذه الأمة باقية لا تنمح ولا تتغير إلى يوم القيامة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further statement says this gift belonged only to this community.
rows.anchor: وقيل: لم يكن إلا هذه الأمة

rows.speaker: ذو النون
rows.claim: Dhu al-Nūn frames completion as four gifts: scripture, the greatest messenger, an honorific grant rather than a loan, and authority enduring until the Trumpet.
rows.anchor: أربعة أشياء: الكتاب والرسول، والخلعة والولاية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Completing the blessing fulfilled God's promise; it included safe entry into Mecca, victory there, and a secure pilgrimage without polytheists, completing the promise to perfect the blessing.
rows.anchor: وأتممت عليكم نعمتي حققت وعدي في قولي ولأتم نعمتي عليكم

rows.speaker: الشعبي
rows.claim: Al-Shaʿbī says the verse descended at ʿArafa as pagan monuments and rites collapsed, polytheism disappeared, and no polytheist joined or circumambulated the House.
rows.anchor: وقال الشعبي: نزلت هذا الآية بعرفات حيث هدم منار الجاهلية ومناسكهم واضمحل الشرك

rows.speaker: ابن عمر
rows.claim: Ibn ʿUmar reports that the Prophet loudly ordered dogs killed; people killed dogs encountered with a woman coming from Madina, and the Prophet prohibited their sale price.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عمر: سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول رافعا صوته

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: Abū Hurayra reports the Prophet's prohibition on the price of dogs, a soothsayer's fee, and a prostitute's earnings.
rows.anchor: عن أبي هريرة قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet also prohibited keeping dogs and ordered washing a vessel licked by one seven times, the first with soil.
rows.anchor: ونهى عن اقتنائها وإمساكها وأمر بغسل الإناء من ولوغها سبع مرات أولاهن بالتراب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After people asked what dog-caught prey remained lawful, the verse permitted useful dogs, forbade keeping useless ones, ordered harmful or rabid dogs killed, and spared harmless dogs.
rows.anchor: فسكت رسول الله فأنزل الله هذه الآية وأذن رسول الله في اقتناء الكلاب التي ينتفع بها

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن معقل
rows.claim: A report from ʿAbd Allāh b. Maʿqil says the Prophet ordered killing solid-black dogs and said keeping dogs except for crops, hunting, or livestock reduces the reward by one qirāṭ daily.
rows.anchor: وروى الحسن عن عبد الله بن معقل قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: Saʿīd b. al-Musayyib transmits from Abū Hurayra that keeping a dog for other than hunting, livestock, or land costs two qirāṭs of reward daily.
rows.anchor: عن سعيد بن المسيب عن أبي هريرة عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال

rows.speaker: عمرو بن عبيد
rows.claim: Asked why a nonworking dog reduces reward, ʿAmr b. ʿUbayd explains that it barks at guests and frightens petitioners.
rows.anchor: قال: خذها بحقها إنما ذلك لأنه ينبح على الضيف ويروع السائل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Generous Arabs disliked and condemned tethering dogs because dogs barked at guests and frightened petitioners, and they wanted to kill them.
rows.anchor: وكانت أسخياء العرب تبغض الكلاب لهذا المعنى وتذم من ربطه وهم بقتله

rows.speaker: بعض شعراء البصرة
rows.claim: An unnamed Basran poet jokes that the dogs at ʿAmmār's lodging nearly devoured the visitors, illustrating the social nuisance of barking dogs.
rows.anchor: أن بعض شعراء البصرة نزل بعمار فسمع لكلابه نبحا فأنشأ يقول

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
rows.claim: Saʿīd b. Jubayr says the verse was revealed about ʿAdī b. Ḥātim and Zayd al-Khayl, later named Zayd al-Khayr, who asked about hunting dogs and falcons.
rows.anchor: قال عطاء بن دينار عن سعيد بن جبير في هذه الآية قال

rows.speaker: عدي بن حاتم وزيد الخير
rows.claim: The two hunters asked about prey caught by their dogs and falcons: some animals could be slaughtered in time, while others died before they could be slaughtered, though carrion was forbidden.
rows.anchor: قالا: يا رسول الله إنا قوم نصيد الكلاب والبزاة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the verse, الطيبات means lawful slaughtered animals, and ما علمتم means prey caught by trained hunting animals.
rows.anchor: فنزلت يسئلونك يا محمد ماذا أحل لهم قل: أحل لكم الطيبات يعني الذبائح التي أحلها الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One view permits only prey reached in time for slaughter and forbids prey killed beyond reach; the author says this position is not acted upon.
rows.anchor: وما أدركت فما ذكاته فهو لك، وإلا فلا يطعم، وهذا غير معمول به

rows.speaker: سائر العلماء
rows.claim: Other scholars define lawful trained predators broadly as teachable hunting beasts and birds, including big cats, dogs, eagles, falcons, hawks, and saker falcons.
rows.anchor: وقال سائر العلماء: هي الكواسب من السباع والبهائم والطير مثل النمر والفهد والكلب والعقاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Predators are called jawāriḥ because they earn their owners' food from prey; the same root describes an earner supporting a family.
rows.anchor: فسميت جوارح لجرحها أربابها أقواتهم من الصيد أي كسبها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The accusative مكلبين describes the state of hunting with trained dogs; taklīb means inciting or setting the animal onto prey.
rows.anchor: مكلبين منصوب على الحساب في المعنى وصيد ما علمتم من الجوارح مكلبين إلى هذه الحال

rows.speaker: الشاعر
rows.claim: An unnamed poet's phrase مكلب for a dawn hunter with a grey wolf-like hound supports the trained-hunter sense.
rows.anchor: قال الشاعر: باكره عند الصباح مكلب … أزل كسرحان القصيمة أغبر

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود وأبو زرين والحسن
rows.claim: Ibn Masʿūd, Abū Zurayn, and al-Ḥasan read مكلبين with a light lām, in the sense of training or urging the hunting animal.
rows.anchor: قرأ أبن مسعود وأبو زرين والحسن: مكلبين بتخفيف اللام على هذا المعنى

rows.speaker: الحسن والقتيبي
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan and al-Qutaybī also derive the word from أكلب, meaning someone acquired many dogs; dogs are named because they are most common, while all trained predators are intended.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون من قولهم: أكلب الرجل، إذا كثرت كلابه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Training the hunting animals means teaching them the manners of hunting from the knowledge God has taught.
rows.anchor: تعلمونهن آداب الصيد مما علمكم الله أي من العلم الذي علمكم الله

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddī reads من as meaning 'as': God taught that trained animals should not lie down on prey, bite, kill, or eat it.
rows.anchor: وقال السدي: من بمعنى الكاف، أي كما علمكم الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command to eat what the animals catch is paired with invoking God's name when releasing the animals or hunting beasts.
rows.anchor: فكلوا مما أمسكن عليكم واذكروا اسم الله عليه عند إرسال البهم والجوارح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A trained animal responds to release, holds prey without eating, answers its call, and does not flee; repeated performance establishes training.
rows.anchor: إذا أرسله صاحبه وأشلاه استشلى وإذا أخذ أمسك ولم يأكل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Prey held without being eaten is lawful; al-Shāfiʿī's more famous and stronger position forbids prey eaten by the animal because it kept the game for itself.
rows.anchor: فإذا أمسك الصيد ولم يأكل منه جاز أكله، وكان حلالا، فإن أكل منه، فللشافعي فيه قولان

rows.speaker: الحسن وطاوس والشعبي وعطاء والسدي
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan, Ṭāwūs, al-Shaʿbī, ʿAṭāʾ, and al-Suddī share the position that prey eaten by the hunting animal is unlawful.
rows.anchor: وهذا قول الحسن وطاوس والشعبي وعطاء والسدي

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says game eaten by a released dog is carrion because the beast held it for itself and was not trained; he says to beat the dog and not eat the prey.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: إذا أرسلت الكلب فأكل من صيد فهي ميتة لا يحل أكله

rows.speaker: عدي بن حاتم
rows.claim: In a report from ʿAdī b. Ḥātim, the Prophet says to invoke God when releasing a dog, slaughter prey found alive, eat prey it killed without eating, and avoid prey it ate or that other dogs may have killed.
rows.anchor: يدل عليه ما روى الشعبي عن عدي بن حاتم أنه سأل رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم عن الصيد

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The same report says to invoke God when shooting an arrow, avoid an animal that died in water because its cause of death is uncertain, and permits eating it if found later with no arrow visible.
rows.anchor: وإذا رميت سهمك فاذكر اسم الله، فإن أدركته فكل، إلا أن تجده وقع في ماء فمات

rows.speaker: سلمان الفارسي وسعد بن أبي وقاص وابن عمر وأبو هريرة
rows.claim: The second Shāfiʿī position permits prey even when the trained animal eats; it is attributed to Salmān, Saʿd b. Abī Waqqāṣ, Ibn ʿUmar, and Abū Hurayra.
rows.anchor: وهو قول سلمان الفارسي، وسعد بن أبي وقاص، وابن عمر، وأبي هريرة

rows.speaker: سعد بن أبي وقاص
rows.claim: Saʿd says his fierce hunting dogs eat from their catch and that one may eat what remains, even if only half or two-thirds is left.
rows.anchor: قال حميد بن عبد الله وسعد ابن أبي وقاص: لنا كلاب ضواري يأكلن ويبقين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The rule applies equally to trained birds and predatory beasts.
rows.anchor: ولا فرق في حمله على ما ذكرنا من الطيور والسباع المعلمة

rows.speaker: ثعلبة الخشني
rows.claim: Thaʿlaba al-Khushanī asks about arrows, trained dogs, and untrained dogs; the Prophet permits what an arrow or trained dog catches with God's name, while an untrained dog's catch is lawful only if reached and slaughtered.
rows.anchor: وروى أبو قلابة عن ثعلبة الخشني: أنه جاء إلى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: يا رسول الله إن أرضنا أرض صيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The permitted good things include slaughtered animals; the food of Jews, Christians, and those who joined their religion before Muhammad's mission is lawful, unlike converts after it.
rows.anchor: اليوم أحل لكم الطيبات يعني الذبائح وطعام الذين أوتوا الكتاب حل لكم يعني ذبائح اليهود والنصارى

rows.speaker: ابن عمر
rows.claim: Ibn ʿUmar, as relayed by Rabīʿa, says not to eat Christian slaughter because Christians invoke Christ; he cites the prohibition on food over which God's name was not mentioned.
rows.anchor: فقال ربيعة: سمعت ابن عمر يقول: لا تأكلوا ذبائح النصارى، فإنهم يقولون: باسم المسيح

rows.speaker: أكثر العلماء
rows.claim: Most scholars permit a scripturalist's slaughter even when another name is invoked, treating the prohibition as directed at polytheists sacrificing to idols.
rows.anchor: والقول الثاني: إنه يجوز ذبيحتهم، الكتابي، وإن سمي غير الله فإن هذا مستثنى

rows.speaker: الشعبي وعطاء
rows.claim: Al-Shaʿbī and ʿAṭāʾ permit a Christian's slaughter when the Christian says 'in the name of Christ,' since God allowed their food and knows what they say.
rows.anchor: قال الشعبي وعطاء: في النصراني يذبح فيقول: باسم المسيح قالا: يحل

rows.speaker: الزهري ومكحول
rows.claim: Al-Zuhrī and Makḥūl say the slaughter of scripturalist worshippers and offerings made for their churches is lawful, citing this verse.
rows.anchor: وسأل الزهري ومكحول عن ذبائح عبدة أهل الكتاب

rows.speaker: الحسن والحرث العكلي
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan and al-Ḥārith al-ʿAklī say not to eat if one hears a Jew or Christian name another than God, but to eat if absent; they regard such slaughter as disliked.
rows.anchor: وقال الحسن والحرث العكلي: ما كنت أسأله عن ذبحه فإنه أحل الله لنا طعامه

rows.speaker: علي
rows.claim: ʿAlī says Jews and Christians should not slaughter Muslims' sacrificial offerings; only a Muslim should slaughter the ritual sacrifice.
rows.anchor: قال علي (رضي الله عنه)

rows.speaker: مجاهد وأكثر الفقهاء
rows.claim: Mujāhid and most jurists interpret ihṣān here as free status: a Muslim may marry any free woman, Muslim or scripturalist, even if sinful, but may never marry scripturalist slave women.
rows.anchor: وهذا قول مجاهد وأكثر الفقهاء، والدليل عليه قوله: ومن لم يستطع منكم طولا الآية
